name: Bagaduce Lunch
season: summer only; opened May 14 for 2026, generally through Labor Day
founded_note: Sid and Bernice Snow opened it in 1946 above the Bagaduce River's reversing falls; Sid Snow's original shack was replaced on the same site by the current, larger building in 2010. The owner says it has always been in a small section of Penobscot between Brooksville and Sedgwick (an old postcard calls it North Brooksville).
note: Counter-service seafood shack with picnic tables over the Bagaduce River reversing falls, run by the same family for three generations; James Beard America's Classics honoree in 2008.

name: Beal's Lobster Pier
season: restaurant closed from October to May; opened May 15 in 2025
founded_note: Working fish and lobster pier since 1932; the Beal family opened the restaurant on the pier in 1969 (its own history page).
note: Restaurant on a year-round working lobster pier on Southwest Harbor, where lobstermen unload their catch beside the tables; it also ships lobster nationwide.

name: Trenton Bridge Lobster Pound
dishes: lobster boiled in seawater over wood fires
season: dine-in June 21 to October 25, 2026; retail pickup and shipping year-round
founded_note: Its site: 'Since 1956, our family has been providing a true traditional Maine experience in eating lobster and clams' (it does not say whether 1956 was at this spot).
note: Roadside pound on Route 3 just before the bridge to Mount Desert Island, with a row of wood-fired seawater cookers out front and a 'LOBSTERS' sign on the roof.

name: Gateway Lunt's Lobster Pound
season: open daily May to October; opened May 6, 2026
note: Traditional lobster pound on Route 3 across from the Bar Harbor airport.

name: Thurston's Lobster Pound
founded_note: The wharf's wholesale lobster business dates to 1946; Michael and Elizabeth Radcliffe added the restaurant in 1993 (leased to a longtime employee 2006-2012).
note: Wharf-top lobster pound under yellow awnings over Bass Harbor, where boats unload the day's catch.

name: Abel's Lobster
season: May 17 to October 20 per its page (year not given); opened May 15 in 2025
founded_note: Mainebiz (2020): 'in operation since 1939' in the Henry R. Abel & Co. boatyard on Somes Sound.
note: Seasonal lobster pound and clam house with a dining room and waterfront seating in Abel's boatyard near the head of Somes Sound.

name: Stewman's Lobster Pound
season: typically early June to early October; opened Memorial Day weekend in 2025
note: Oceanfront lobster pound on the downtown Bar Harbor waterfront serving lobster bakes; a second Stewman's is at the Bar Harbor Regency.

name: Stewman's Lobster Pound (Bar Harbor Regency)
season: typically early June to early October; opened Memorial Day weekend in 2025
branch_of: Stewman's Lobster Pound, Bar Harbor (35 West St)
note: The second, oceanfront Stewman's, on the grounds of the Bar Harbor Regency hotel on Eden Street.

name: Ruth & Wimpy's
founded_note: Ruth and Wimpy bought the restaurant in 1990 (its site); its site says 2026 is its 37th year.
note: Family-owned roadside lobster restaurant on Route 1 where Wimpy still cooks the lobsters outside over wood-burning cookers; out front stands 'Wilbur,' an 11-foot fiberglass sculpture by Joe Rizzo.

name: Union River Lobster Pot
note: Seasonal lobster restaurant overlooking the Union River in Ellsworth.

name: LDI Lobster Dock & Dine
founded_note: Began as a sister location of the Boatyard Grill in Blue Hill.
note: Seasonal takeout with outdoor tables on Eggemoggin Reach beside the Deer Isle-Sedgwick Bridge, reachable by land or by sea.

name: Chipman's Wharf
founded_note: Working wharf run by the fourth generation of the Chipman family; its market and lunch grille building was added in 2021.
note: Family working lobster wharf in Milbridge with a seafood market and a daily lunch grille, with tables on the waterfront and an upstairs deck.

name: Fisherman's Wharf Restaurant & Seafood
note: Restaurant of The Inn on the Wharf, in the old boiler room of a former Lubec sardine factory on Passamaquoddy Bay; lobster turns up at every meal.

name: Look Lobster Rolls and Market
season: closing for the 2026 season on October 8
founded_note: Look Lobster replaced the Quoddy Bay lobster shack at this site; the Look family lobster business began on a Jonesport wharf in 1910.
note: Waterfront lobster shack and fish market in Eastport with a deck looking over Passamaquoddy Bay, run by the Jonesport-based Look Lobster Co., which also has sites in Addison and Portland.

name: The Dairy Port
season: opened March 28 for 2026; open daily in season
founded_note: The Maine Magazine (2022): founded in 1954; its own 2024 post said 2024 marked the 70th year of the ice cream parlor on Main Street.
note: Walk-up ice cream window in a narrow historic storefront on Bucksport's Main Street, across from the harbor and the Penobscot Narrows Bridge; known for its daily soft-serve flavors.

name: Polar Treat
season: closing for the 2026 season on October 11
note: Ice cream spot with a full food menu on Route 1 in Perry, near Eastport.

name: Stonington Ice Cream Company
address: Main St (beside Stonington Food Company, 68 Main St)
season: aims for early May to late October; closed before the end of September in 2026 for lack of staff
founded_note: Ron Watson opened it on Main Street in 2008 (BDN, 2026).
note: Harborside ice cream shop on Stonington's Main Street with deck tables at the edge of the harbor; its owner added the Stonington Food Company restaurant next door.

name: Jordan's Snack Bar
founded_note: Its site: 'Serving our community since 1981'; started by Jimmy and Carol Jordan, now owned by Scott and Katie Kenny.
note: Ellsworth snack bar on the Downeast Highway with seafood, burgers and weekly soft-serve specials, a playground and game room, and Wednesday-night cruise-ins.

name: The Stoop Oyster Bar
dishes: Long Cove oysters from Deer Isle Oyster Co.
founded_note: Opened July 2, 2026 in the historic Pendleton House (c. 1826) on Water Street.
note: Oyster bar from Deer Isle Oyster Co. farmer Abby Barrows serving her Long Cove oysters alongside other Downeast farms' oysters, with small plates and a full bar.

name: WaCo Diner
founded_note: Calls itself Maine's oldest diner, since 1924 (its site and the Eastport chamber). The Quoddy Tides says Nelson Watts and Ralph Colwell bought the lunch wagon where it stood near Bank Square in 1923 and named it from their surnames; the first printed mention is April 23, 1924. The cart frame was replaced by the current building around 1970 on the same spot.
note: Downtown Eastport diner with a full bar and a waterfront deck, plus the Schooner Room dining room for dinners.

name: Jordan Pond House
founded_note: Exact year disputed: Wikipedia says Melvan Tibbetts established it as a restaurant in the early 1870s, with Thomas and Nellie McIntire running it from 1895; the National Park Service says it has served tea and popovers since the 1890s. The original building burned on June 21, 1979; the current restaurant building was completed in 1982 on the same site.
note: Acadia National Park's historic tea house and restaurant on the south shore of Jordan Pond, famous for popovers and tea on the lawn facing the Bubbles.

name: The Asticou Hotel
founded_note: Disputed: the hotel says it traces its origins to 1883; a spokesperson told the BDN (2025) it began as a family home boarding lodgers in 1870. It was rebuilt after a 1900 fire and suspended operations during World War II. Closed in 2024 for a $28 million renovation, it reopened in July 2025 and was bought out of bankruptcy by Ocean Properties in 2026.
note: Historic shingled summer hotel above Northeast Harbor whose restaurant, Dahlia's, serves a seasonal menu of local seafood; under new ownership in 2026.

name: Pentagöet Inn
founded_note: Built in 1894; its site calls it Castine's oldest original 'summer hotel' still welcoming guests.
note: Queen Anne Victorian summer hotel in Castine village with a cozy pub and wine bar serving small plates most evenings.
